title: Family handbook 2026–27
summary: Attendance, the bell schedule, buses, lunch, devices and who to call, for every school.
body:
The handbook covers what every family needs in one place: bell times, attendance, buses, lunch, devices and how to reach your school.

Who to call first

  • Your child's teacher, for anything about class
  • The front office, for attendance and pickup
  • The school counselor, for anything that worries you

title: Snow days, delays and early releases: how we decide
summary: Who makes the call, by when, and where it is posted first.
body:
The superintendent decides by 5:30 am after transportation drives the routes. The decision is posted to the status strip on this site first, then sent by text and phone.

What each status means

  • Delayed start: buses and first bell run two hours later
  • Early release: dismissal at 12:45 pm unless the school says otherwise
  • Closed: no school, and no after-school activities

title: Accessibility statement
summary: Our commitment to accessible websites and documents, and how to report a barrier.
body: See the full statement on the accessibility page. Report a barrier to Bettina Okonkwo, accessibility and Section 504 coordinator, at extension 1030.

title: Conference week: what to bring and how long it takes
summary: A twenty-minute conversation: the questions teachers will ask and three you might ask them.
body:
Conferences are twenty minutes. Your child's teacher will share reading and math progress, a work sample, and one goal for the next quarter.

  1. Look at the work sample together first
  2. Ask what a good week looks like at home
  3. Ask who to contact between conferences

Interpreters are available in Spanish, Arabic, Vietnamese and Dari; tell the office two days ahead.

title: Bus stop times after the November 2 route change
summary: Updated morning and afternoon stop times for Ridge line routes 12, 14 and 15.
body: Dear families, starting Monday, November 2 the Ridge line routes change by three to eight minutes. Route 14 now picks up at Marrow St & 5th at 7:14 am (was 7:22). Afternoon drop-off moves to 3:10 pm.

title: Allergy and special diet care plans
summary: How to set up a care plan with the school nurse, and how the kitchen uses it.
body: The nurse meets with families of students with food allergies before the first day, or within a week of a new diagnosis. The kitchen receives the plan and marks the student's account so cashiers see a prompt at the register.

title: Staff bulletin: week of October 26
summary: Conference week schedules, the Quarry Hill delay plan, and the November 24 accessibility training.
body:
Conference week: elementary staff, please confirm interpreter requests with the front office by Friday. Quarry Hill staff report at 9:20 am on delay days.

November 24 training: bring one document you share with families; we will make it accessible together.

title: Substitute procedures
summary: How to request a substitute, what to leave, and the sub plan template.
body:
Request through the absence system by 5:30 am. Leave a sub folder with the bell schedule, seating chart, emergency procedures and a plan for every period.

  1. Bell schedule and duty times
  2. Seating chart and student support notes
  3. Emergency procedures card

title: Emergency procedures quick card
summary: Lockdown, shelter, evacuate, and reunification: the four steps, on one card.
body:
Post this card by every classroom door. Practice dates are set by each principal (story).

  • Lockdown: locks, lights, out of sight
  • Shelter: to the designated area for weather
  • Evacuate: to the assembly point with your roster
  • Reunify: release students only at the reunification table

title: Making documents accessible before you post them
summary: Headings, alt text, contrast and tables: a checklist for anything you post to this site or send home.
body: Use real headings, write alt text that says what an image shows, keep text contrast high, and use table headers. Scanned PDFs are not accessible; post the text instead.
